newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products - Gasoline diffs gain modestly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products - Gasoline diffs gain modestly.

text.p: U.S. gasoline differentials firmed modestly Tuesday, with U.S. Gulf levels helped by the explosion that shut an alkylation unit at Citgo's Corpus Christi, Texas refinery.
On the NYMEX, June gasoline settled 0.29 cent higher, while June heating oil futures shed 0.17 cent.
- U.S. GULF

++ GASOLINE: Prompt conventional M1 differentials were talked higher early in the day, helped by the fire at the Citgo facility, though the one confirmed deal at 3.60 cents under the June futures put the increase at about 0.10 cent.

"The NYMEX got excited about (Citgo) early but then sold off," one products trader said. "It's really a non-issue at this point. It's a matter of whether Citgo comes into the spot market buying barrels" to replace lost output, the trader added.

Market players said the conventional M-grades should not see any strength on the Citgo outage, though the reformulated and premium gasolines may find some additional buying, since those grade utilize akylates.

Offers on the normally thinly-traded "V1" summer grade premium fuel popped up 0.25 cent in the early going Tuesday to 4.50 cents over "M1" U.S. Gulf Coast regular unleaded on supplies for prompt delivery.
++ DISTILLATES: Prompt heating oil differentials weakened slightly, with barrels talked at about 2.25 cents under the June futures, about 0.25 cent under the June futures.
- NEW YORK HARBOR
++ DISTILLATES: Heating oil differentials eased, with players reporting prompt barrels changing hands at even with the June NYMEX price, down more than 0.25 cent from Monday's levels.
Low sulphur diesel differentials also weakened, with prompt barrels quoted between about 0.75 and 0.85 cent over the June futures.
++ GASOLINE: Offers for prompt conventional M1 barrels firmed slightly to 1.25 cents under the June futures, while barrels for delivery by May 20th changed hands at 1.65 cents under the June futures.
MIDCONTINENT
Chicago conventional unleaded gasoline diffs widened 1.25 cents by Tuesday afternoon to 2.75 cents over the June print as buyers scrambled to cover their short positions amid tight supplies.

And Group Three conventional unleaded differentials firmed one cent to 5.0 cents over on spirited short-covering, players said, related to expected delays in receiving 14th-cycle material from the Gulf Coast via the Explorer Pipeline.
"A lot of people are having to pay up to cover by the 20th of the month," one Group Three player said.
Group Three low sulfur diesel, meanwhile, saw differentials hold steady from Monday's levels, with offers at 6.0 cents over the June print.

- CARGOES: Traders said they saw relatively few gasoline cargoes on offer to the U.S. compared to volumes seen in recent weeks, despite the wide-open arbitrage window between Europe and the U.S. East Coast.
"There's significantly less (on offer) than what we usually see. There's some drips and drops but not that much," one East Coast player said.
